sources.title: SteamDB - app 317800 'Double Action Dedicated Server', type Tool, Source engine (store-retired)
Steam Support - Double Action Dedicated Server (app 317800)
Official Server Setup Guide (Double Action Steam guide) - 'srcds -game dab +maxplayers 10'
Server Setup Guide - Windows (Double Action Steam group) - 'srcds -game dab'
LinuxGSM dabserver _default.cfg (appid 317800, engine source, port 27015, defaultmap da_rooftops)
Valve Developer Community - Source Dedicated Server (27015 TCP/UDP carries RCON; server.cfg in <game>/cfg/)
Valve Developer Community - Console Command List (kick, banid, addip, removeid, removeip, listid, say, rcon_password)
Valve Developer Community - List of TF2 console commands (kickid: 'Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message')
Official TF2 Wiki - Dedicated server configuration (rcon_password in server.cfg, exec banned_user.cfg / banned_ip.cfg, writeid, writeip)
Official TF2 Wiki - List of useful console commands (banid <minutes> <steamid>, 0 = permanent; kick <name>; status)

notes: Stock Source SDK 2013 dedicated server: SteamDB and Steam Support name app 317800 'Double Action Dedicated Server' (Source engine, since retired from the store), LinuxGSM's dabserver _default.cfg records appid 317800, engine=source, port 27015, and both developer-side setup guides launch it as 'srcds -game dab', so the command set is the engine's, not the mod's. No DAB-specific page documents any admin command; every command here is the stock Source form, sourced from Valve's own wiki and the official TF2 wiki. RCON rides the TCP game port (27015 by default, moved with -port; LinuxGSM passes -port in startparameters) and is enabled simply by setting rcon_password in dab/cfg/server.cfg - no separate enable or port setting. Per-command sourcing, so a reader knows what is thin: banid, removeid, say, kick and rcon_password appear on Valve's Console Command List; kickid ('Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message') appears only on Valve's TF2 console-command list; banid's ARGUMENT ORDER and its units - 'banid <minutes> <steamid>', 0 meaning permanent - come from exactly ONE source, the TF2 wiki, since Valve's own list gives no syntax; removeid's argument form is inferred from its description. An earlier draft of this file claimed Valve's engine help documents an optional trailing 'kick' argument ('banid <minutes> <id> [kick]') - that could not be found in any source and has been removed; the two-argument form recorded here is the only one with a source. banid holds the ban in memory only: run 'writeid' to commit it to banned_user.cfg (TF2 wiki), and banid does not disconnect an already-connected player, so kick separately. kickid and banid both accept either the in-session userid from 'status' (captured as accountId) or the Steam ID; the Steam ID is recorded as playerId because it is what the ban list persists. No source shows a real 'status' dump from this build, and Source prints the uniqueid column as STEAM_0:1:x on older builds and [U:1:x] on 2013-era builds, so the pattern and the parse accept both - the parse is therefore unconfirmed against real output. IP bans use the parallel addip/removeip/writeip and banned_ip.cfg. No motd command exists - Source serves motd.txt from the game directory - so no motd key. Nothing here has been run against a live server.
